recipe_version.title: Pakistani Lamb Keema Matar with Green Peas and Warm Chapatis
recipe_version.description: Ground lamb cooked down with browned onions, garlic, ginger, green chiles, and tomatoes in cumin seeds, coriander, Kashmiri chile, turmeric, and yogurt until dry and fragrant, folded with green peas and garam masala, finished with cilantro, and scooped up with warm chapatis.

ingredients.name: chapatis
ingredients.display_name: whole wheat chapatis whose label lists whole wheat flour, water, oil, and salt

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Finely chop the onions and tomatoes, grate the garlic and ginger, slit the chiles, and chop the cilantro. Stir the yogurt smooth.

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.body: Heat the oil in the 12-inch deep skillet over medium-high, about 1 minute. Add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onions, and cook, stirring, until golden brown, about 9 minutes.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.body: Add the garlic, ginger, and chiles for 1 minute, then the lamb, breaking it up, until no pink remains, about 7 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.body: Stir in the tomatoes, coriander, chile powder, turmeric, and salt and cook until the tomatoes break down, about 6 minutes. Lower the heat to medium, stir in the yogurt a spoonful at a time, cover, and simmer 8 minutes, then uncover and cook, stirring, until dry and the oil separates, about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Peas
steps.body: Stir in the peas and garam masala and cook until the peas are tender, about 4 minutes. Scatter with cilantro.

steps.title: Warm the chapatis
steps.body: Warm each chapati in the dry 10-inch skillet over medium, about 30 seconds per side, and stack them in the clean kitchen towel. Serve with the keema.

coverage_contribution: South Asian meat dinners in the catalog are chicken karahi and butter chicken; there is no lamb curry or keema. A fast ground-lamb dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with pakistani-chicken-karahi: dry-cooked ground lamb with peas, not chicken in a tomato-ginger karahi. Compared with south-african-bobotie: a stovetop masala eaten with chapatis, not a baked curried mince under egg custard. Compared with punjabi-rajma-chawal: a ground-lamb curry, not a kidney bean curry with rice.
not_duplicate_of: Not shepherd's pie and not aloo keema (no potato). Unlike lebanese-arayes in this wave, the lamb is curried and eaten loose with bread, not stuffed into pita.
